title: CBSE CLASS 3 — Mathematics | Circles Tangents
description: Subject-wise test on Circles Tangents (Mathematics) for CBSE CLASS 3. 25Q.
subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Which of the following shapes is a circle?

options.explanation: A square has four straight sides and four corners.
A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.
A circle is round with no straight sides or corners.
A rectangle has four straight sides and four corners.

questions.explanation: A circle is a round shape with no corners or straight sides. Option C represents a circle.
questions.hint: Look for a shape with no straight edges or corners.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Which of these objects found in your home is shaped like a circle?

options.explanation: A book is usually rectangular with straight sides.
A door is typically rectangular with straight sides.
A dinner plate is round and has the shape of a circle.
A ruler is long and straight, usually rectangular.

questions.explanation: A dinner plate is typically round and has the shape of a circle. Books, doors, and rulers usually have straight sides and corners (rectangular shapes).
questions.hint: Think of objects that are round in shape.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: How many straight sides does a circle have?

options.explanation: A circle does not have any straight sides.
A circle does not have any straight sides.
A circle does not have any straight sides.
A circle has no straight sides, only a curved boundary.

questions.explanation: A circle is a completely round shape and does not have any straight sides. It has only one curved boundary.
questions.hint: A circle is smooth and round all around.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: What is the special point exactly in the middle of a circle called?

options.explanation: A corner is where two straight lines meet, which a circle does not have.
The edge of a circle is its curved boundary, not a single point.
The center is the point in the middle of a circle, equidistant from all points on its boundary.
A circle does not have sides.

questions.explanation: The point that is equally far from all points on the boundary of a circle is called its center.
questions.hint: Think of the middle point of a circle.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: If you use a bangle to draw a shape on paper, what shape will you get?

options.explanation: A square has straight sides and corners.
A triangle has three straight sides.
Tracing a bangle will produce a circular shape.
A rectangle has four straight sides and four corners.

questions.explanation: Bangles are circular in shape. Tracing their outline will produce a circle on paper. This is a common way for children to draw circles.
questions.hint: Bangles are round objects.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Ria drew two circles. One circle was drawn using a small bottle cap, and the other was drawn using a big dinner plate. Which circle will be bigger?

options.text: The circle drawn with the bottle cap
options.explanation: A bottle cap is small, so the circle drawn will be small.

options.text: The circle drawn with the dinner plate
options.explanation: A dinner plate is large, so the circle drawn will be large.

options.text: Both circles will be the same size
options.explanation: The sizes depend on the objects used to trace them.

options.text: It depends on the color of the cap and plate
options.explanation: The size depends on the physical size of the objects, not their color.

questions.explanation: The size of the circle drawn depends on the size of the object used to trace it. A big dinner plate is larger than a small bottle cap, so the circle drawn with the plate will be bigger.
questions.hint: Larger objects will produce larger circles when traced.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Look at the picture. (Imagine a picture showing a wheel of a bicycle). What is the shape of the bicycle wheel?

options.explanation: An oval is elongated, not perfectly round like a circle.
A square has straight sides and corners.
A bicycle wheel is round and has the shape of a circle.
A triangle has three straight sides.

questions.explanation: A bicycle wheel is designed to be perfectly round, which is the shape of a circle, to allow for smooth movement.
questions.hint: Bicycle wheels are round.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a circle is TRUE?

options.explanation: A circle has no corners.
A circle is made up of a single curved line.
A circle has no straight sides.

options.text: It can be folded into a triangle.
options.explanation: Folding a circle cannot create a triangle.

questions.explanation: A circle is defined by its single, continuous curved line that forms its boundary. It does not have corners or straight sides.
questions.hint: A circle is smooth and has no straight edges.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Sunita says, 'A coin is a circle.' Her friend Amit says, 'A coin has a flat surface, so it cannot be a circle.' Who is correct and why?

options.text: Amit is correct because circles are always thin.
options.explanation: Circles can be part of 3D objects like coins, and their faces are circular.

options.text: Sunita is correct because the face of a coin is round.
options.explanation: The face of a coin is a perfect circle, even though the coin itself is a cylinder.

options.text: Both are correct because a coin is a special type of circle.
options.explanation: A coin is not a circle itself but has circular faces.

options.text: Neither is correct, a coin is a cylinder.
options.explanation: While a coin is a cylinder, its face is a circle, which is what Sunita is referring to.

questions.explanation: While a coin is a 3D object (a cylinder), its top and bottom faces are perfect circles. For Class 3, identifying the circular face is the correct understanding. Amit's reasoning about 'flat surface' is irrelevant to the shape of the face itself.
questions.hint: Think about the shape of the face of the coin, not the entire object.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: You want to draw a perfect circle without using a compass. Which of these methods would work best?

options.text: Using a ruler to draw straight lines.
options.explanation: A ruler is used to draw straight lines, not circles.

options.text: Tracing the outline of a round object like a cup.
options.explanation: Tracing a round object like a cup will produce a perfect circle.

options.text: Drawing freehand with a pencil and hoping it's round.
options.explanation: Freehand drawing rarely produces a perfect circle.

options.text: Folding a square paper in half.
options.explanation: Folding paper creates straight edges, not a circle.

questions.explanation: For Class 3 students, tracing a circular object (like a cup, coin, or bangle) is the most effective and accurate way to draw a perfect circle without specialized tools like a compass. Drawing freehand is usually not perfect, and a ruler or folding paper creates shapes with straight edges.
questions.hint: Think of tools or objects that can help you draw a smooth, round shape.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

options.explanation: This describes a square.

options.explanation: This describes a rectangle.

A triangle has three straight sides.

A wheel is circular in shape.

questions.explanation: A wheel is a common real-world example of a circular shape.

questions.question: A line segment that connects the center of a circle to any point on its boundary is called a:

options.explanation: A diameter passes through the center and connects two points on the boundary.
This is the correct term for the line segment from the center to the boundary.
A chord connects two points on the boundary but does not necessarily pass through the center.
A tangent touches the circle at only one point but does not connect the center to the boundary.

questions.explanation: The radius is defined as the distance from the center of the circle to any point on its circumference.
questions.hint: This line segment starts from the center and ends at the edge of the circle.

questions.question: How many complete circles can you count in the image of a smiley face made of circles (one large circle for the face, two smaller circles for eyes, and one tiny circle for the nose)?

options.explanation: There are more than two circles in the image.
There are four circles in the image.
There are four complete circles in the image.
There are only four circles in the image.

questions.explanation: Counting the shapes: 1 large circle for the face, 2 smaller circles for the eyes, and 1 tiny circle for the nose. Total = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 complete circles.
questions.hint: Look for all the circular shapes in the image.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Assertion: A circle is a closed curve. Reason: It starts and ends at the same point if you trace its boundary without lifting your pencil. Which of the following statements is true about the Assertion and Reason?

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation for the Assertion.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation for the Assertion.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: A closed curve is one that can be drawn without lifting the pencil and ends at the same point where it started. A circle perfectly fits this description, making both the assertion and the reason true, and the reason correctly explains why a circle is a closed curve.
questions.hint: Think about the definition of a closed curve.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: A diameter of a circle is a line segment that passes through the center and connects two points on the boundary. If the radius of a circle is 5 cm, what would be its diameter?

options.explanation: The diameter is twice the radius.
The diameter is 10 cm.
The diameter is twice the radius.
The diameter is twice the radius.

questions.explanation: The diameter of a circle is always twice its radius. Calculation: Diameter = 2 × Radius = 2 × 5 cm = 10 cm.
questions.hint: Remember that the diameter is twice the radius.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Rohan wants to draw different circles on a sheet of paper. He uses a small coin, a bangle, and a dinner plate. Which object will help Rohan draw the largest circle?

options.explanation: A small coin will draw the smallest circle.
A bangle will draw a medium-sized circle.
A dinner plate will draw the largest circle.

options.text: All three will draw circles of the same size.
options.explanation: The circles will be of different sizes.

questions.explanation: The size of the circle drawn depends on the size of the circular object used. Among a small coin, a bangle, and a dinner plate, the dinner plate has the largest circular edge, and thus will draw the largest circle.
questions.hint: Think about the size of the objects Rohan is using.
questions.subject: cbse3-maths

questions.question: Look at the figure below: A circle with its center marked 'O'. A straight line 'AB' is drawn such that it touches the circle at only one point, say 'P', on the circumference, and does not cross inside the circle. What can you say about the line AB and the circle?

options.text: The line AB goes through the center of the circle.
options.explanation: This would describe a diameter.

options.text: The line AB passes completely inside the circle.
options.explanation: This would describe a chord.

options.text: The line AB touches the circle at only one point.
options.explanation: This describes a tangent line.

options.text: The line AB cuts the circle at two different points.
options.explanation: This would describe a secant line.

questions.explanation: Based on the description, the line AB is drawn to touch the circle at exactly one point on its boundary without entering the interior. Options A, B, and D describe different relationships (diameter/chord, chord, secant, respectively), which are not what is described for line AB.
questions.hint: Think about how the line AB interacts with the circle.

questions.question: Anya wants to draw a big circle and a small circle. She uses a bangle to trace one circle and a button to trace another. Which object will help her draw the bigger circle?

options.text: Both will draw circles of the same size.
options.explanation: A bangle and a button are of different sizes.

options.text: The button will draw the bigger circle.
options.explanation: A button is smaller than a bangle.

options.text: The bangle will draw the bigger circle.
options.explanation: A bangle is larger than a button, so it will draw a bigger circle.

options.text: It depends on how hard Anya presses.
options.explanation: The size of the circle depends on the size of the object, not the pressure applied.

questions.explanation: A bangle is generally much larger than a button. When Anya traces the outline of a bangle, the circle formed will be larger than the circle formed by tracing a button. Therefore, the bangle will help her draw the bigger circle.
